Clarias pachynema Boulenger, 1903. Type locality: Ja River, southern Cameroon. Maximum size: 356 mm (14 in) SL. IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2019).

Etymology: Clarias comes from the Greek chlaros, meaning lively, in reference to the ability of the fish to live for long periods out of water.

Identification: Clarias species have an elongated body; a soft-rayed dorsal fin extending to, or nearly to, the caudal fin base; a soft-rayed anal fin extending from just behind the anus to the caudal fin base; pectoral fins each with a serrated anterior bony spine; a depressed head covered largely by firmly sutured, surface-sculptured bony plates forming a protective helmet; four pairs of flagellate barbels; and air-breathing organs derived from the 2nd and 4th epibranchials within a superbranchial chamber. In this species the head is pointed in dorsal outline, the snout is short and the eyes are dorsally located. The frontal fontanelle is long and narrow (knife-shaped) and the occipital process is long and oval. The dermosphenotic and supraorbital bones are joined in specimens over 80 mm SL. Tooth plates are small, gill rakers are long, slender and distantly set, and the suprabranchial organ is well developed. Openings of the secondary sensory canals are regularly arranged on the flanks.
Africa: coastal rivers of south Cameroon (up to the Sanaga River); in the Ogowe system in Gabon and the Middle Congo system (including the Sangha and Dja/Ngoko).
Suggested tankmates: large cyprinids (for example Silver Sharks, Tinfoil or Spanner Barbs) or Central American cichlids.

The genital papilla, which is to the right of the anus when viewing the fish with its head to the left, is elongated and pointed in males, while it is round and relatively larger (and larger than the anus) in females. In ventral view especially, females are much broader in the body than males of equal age and rearing practices.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.
Fishbase lists 356 mm TL. Synonyms: Clarias esamesae, Clarias oxycephalus.
Annals and Magazine of Natural History (Series 7) v. 12 (no. 70) (art. 42), pp 438.
